appraisal_events.evidence: elle m'avait tout caché... Il y avait une seule chose qu'elle ne ferait jamais plus pour moi... c'était précisément avouer. J'en serais réduit pour toujours, comme un juge, à tirer des conclusions incertaines... Et toujours elle me sentirait jaloux et juge.
appraisal_events.explanation: Once open and confiding with the narrator, Albertine has become permanently guarded, withholding avowal and controlling what he can know, while he is left dependent on uncertain inference; the passage marks a durable shift of emotional leverage toward her, at the cost of their former intimacy.

appraisal_events.evidence: elle s'était crue méprisée par le fils, avait cherché quelque chose qui pourrait l'embarrasser, lui faire honte, avait inventé tout un roman de dépositions qu'elle était imaginairement appelée à faire
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly exposes Andrée's nervous jealousy and malice, revealing that she invented a slanderous story about an innocent man's father purely out of wounded vanity.

status_effects.explanation: Albertine gains lasting control in the relation by withholding confidences and refusing to explain herself, leaving the narrator permanently reduced to suspicion and inference.
Andrée is clearly diminished in the narrator's judgment as petty, envious, and willing to fabricate a damaging falsehood out of spite.

ambiguities: Albertine's turn to secrecy is narrated ambiguously: the narrator attributes the change to his own jealousy having provoked it, so it is unclear whether her withholding reflects concealment of wrongdoing or simple self-protective discretion.
